item.title: 1996: Yankees Beat Braves 3-2, Win 1996 World Series
item.description: The New York Yankees take their fourth victory in a row from the Atlanta Braves, 3-2, giving them the 1996 World Series and their 23rd World Championship. Starter Jimmy Key gets the win with help from closer John Wetteland, whose four saves earn him the World Series MVP trophy.

item.title: 2018: Muncy's Lead-off Walk-off Homer Lifts Dodgers Over Red Sox in 18
item.description: Max Muncy hit a lead-off, walk-off home run against Nathan Eovaldi in the bottom of the 18th inning, to give the Los Angeles Dodgers a 3–2 victory over the Boston Red Sox in Game 3 of the World Series at Dodger Stadium. Photo: Ian D'Andrea (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2017: Yankees Won't Bring Back Joe Girardi as Manager for 2018
item.description: The New York Yankees announced they would not bring Joe Girardi back as their manager in 2018, following a season in which he oversaw a young team that came within a game of the World Series. The Yankees had notified the previous week that Girardi would not return as manager in 2018, opting instead to allow his contract to expire. Photo: Girardi in 2020 (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 2015: Stottlemyre Named Mariners Pitching Coach Under Servais
item.description: On October 26, 2015, Stottlemyre was announced as the new pitching coach for the Seattle Mariners during manager Scott Servais' inaugural press conference.

item.title: 2009: Cardinals Rehire Tony La Russa, Hire Mark McGwire as Hitting Coach
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals announce the re-hiring of Tony La Russa as manager for 2010, and the surprise hiring of Mark McGwire as hitting coach, replacing Hal McRae. Photo: Jon Gudorf Photography (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2008: Phillies Pitcher Joe Blanton Homers in World Series Game 4
item.description: Pitcher Joe Blanton of the Phillies hits a home run in Game 4 of the World Series, becoming the first pitcher to hit a home run in the World Series since 1974. Photo: Killervogel5 on en.wikipedia (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 2006: Nippon Ham Fighters Sweep Chunichi Dragons 4-1 in Japan Series
item.description: The Hokkaido Nippon Ham Fighters win their fourth straight game over the Chunichi Dragons, winning the Japan Series 4–1. Photo: Kinori (photographer) (Public domain).

item.title: 2005: White Sox Complete World Series Sweep of Astros With 1-0 Win
item.description: In the World Series, the Chicago White Sox complete a sweep of the Houston Astros with a 1–0 victory in Game Four. Freddy García pitches seven shutout innings, and Series MVP Jermaine Dye connects an RBI single off Brad Lidge in the eighth for the only run of the game, as Juan Uribe adds strong defensive support at shortstop. García becomes the first Venezuelan starting pitcher to win a World Series game. Photo: Fuzzy510 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2005: White Sox Sweep Astros in 2005 World Series, Ending Postseason
item.description: The postseason began on October 4, 2005, and ended on October 26, 2005, with the White Sox sweeping the Astros in the 2005 World Series. Photo: Fuzzy510 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2004: Seibu Lions Beat Chunichi 7-2 in Game 7, Win First Title Since 1992
item.description: Takashi Ishii goes six strong innings and Alex Cabrera hits a towering two-run homer as the Seibu Lions defeat the Chunichi Dragons 7-2 in Game 7 of the Japan Series to win their first championship since 1992. The ball bounces off the glass-enclosed private boxes above the left field seats. It is Cabrera's third home run of the Series.

item.title: 2004: Bobby Ávila, 80, Mexican All-Star Second Baseman
item.description: Bobby Ávila, 80, Mexican All-Star second baseman for the Cleveland Indians who won the AL batting title in 1954, the first Hispanic player to do so; became president of the Mexican League. Photo: Caramelos El Indio (Public domain).

item.title: 2002: Angels Trail 5-0, Stage Stunning Comeback, Force Game 7
item.description: The Anaheim Angels stage one of the great comebacks in World Series history to force a seventh game. With one out in the 7th inning, the Giants are leading 5–0 and are just 8 outs from their first World Series title since moving to San Francisco. But after two singles, Scott Spezio fouls off several pitches before hitting a 3-run homer to get the Angels close. Photo: shgmom56 on Flickr (Original version) User UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2000: Yankees Beat Mets 4-2, Win 26th World Series in Five Games
item.description: The New York Yankees defeat the New York Mets 4–2, to win their 26th World Series in five games. Luis Sojo hits a single in the top of the 9th inning and drives home the winning run for the Yankees. Teammates Bernie Williams and Derek Jeter hit home runs, and Jeter is named the Series MVP.

item.title: 1997: Marlins Beat Indians in Game 7, Win World Series
item.description: The Florida Marlins defeat the Cleveland Indians in Game 7 to win the World Series in just their 5th season of existence. Photo: (WT-de) Mistoffeles (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 1994: Frank Thomas Repeats as American League MVP
item.description: Frank Thomas of the Chicago White Sox repeated as American League MVP as he got 24 of the 28 first-place votes. Photo: clare_and_ben User:Delaywaves (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1991: Bill Bevens, 75, Yankees Pitcher, Game 4 Near No-Hitter
item.description: Bill Bevens, 75, pitcher for the New York Yankees from 1944 to 1947 and also part of the 1947 World Series champion Yankees; famously took a no-hit game into the ninth inning of Game 4 of that Fall Classic, before surrendering a two-out double to Cookie Lavagetto and losing the contest, 3–2.

item.title: 1988: Lasorda Wins NL Manager of the Year, 19 of 24 First-Place Votes
item.description: Six days after leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to an improbable World Series championship, Tommy Lasorda is named NL Manager of the Year by the BBWAA. Lasorda wins in a runaway, taking 19 of 24 first place votes for 101 points, doubling the support for his runner-up, Jim Leyland of the Pittsburgh Pirates. Photo: Series: Reagan White House Photographs, 1/20/1981 - 1/20/1989 (Public domain).

item.title: 1985: Cardinals Lead 1-0 in Ninth, Poised for World Series Title
item.description: With champagne on ice in their clubhouse, the St. Louis Cardinals—ahead 1–0 in the bottom of the ninth of Game 6 at Royals Stadium and three-games-to-two in the 1985 World Series—are poised to capture the franchise's tenth Fall Classic, when an umpire's decision drastically changes momentum. Photo: User Wahkeenah on en.wikipedia (Public domain).

item.title: 1985: Bob Scheffing, 72, Catcher, Manager and Mets General Manager
item.description: Bob Scheffing, 72, catcher, coach, manager and executive; hit .263 with 20 home runs and 187 RBI in 517 games for the Chicago Cubs, Cincinnati Reds and St. Louis Cardinals between 1941 and 1951; managed Cubs from 1957 through 1959 and Detroit Tigers from 1961 until June 16, 1963; succeeded Johnny Murphy as general manager of the New York Mets upon Murphy's sudden death in January 1970, and served as GM through the…

item.title: 1982: Steve Carlton Wins Fourth Cy Young After 23 Victories
item.description: Steve Carlton of the Philadelphia Phillies wins his fourth NL Cy Young Award, after winning 23 games—the only MLB pitcher to exceed 20 victories during 1982. Photo: Peter Bond (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1981: Steinbrenner Injures Hand in Elevator After Game 5 Loss
item.description: George Steinbrenner hits the headlines after his New York Yankees drop Game 5 of the 1981 World Series to the home-standing Dodgers. Riding in an elevator at Los Angeles' Hyatt-Wilshire Hotel, the 51-year-old owner injures his left hand and suffers a cut lip, allegedly after scuffling with two Dodger fans who had ridiculed the Yankees and their fanbase.

item.title: 1977: Cardinals Buy Contract of Pitcher Aurelio López From Mexico City Reds
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals purchase the contract of pitcher Aurelio López from the Mexico City Reds of the Mexican League.

item.title: 1973: Red Sox Trade Reggie Smith to Cardinals for Wise, Carbo
item.description: The Boston Red Sox pull off their third significant trade in four days, dealing two-time All-Star outfielder Reggie Smith and relief pitcher Ken Tatum to the St. Louis Cardinals for starting pitcher Rick Wise and outfielder Bernie Carbo. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1960: American League Adds Los Angeles, Moves Senators to Minneapolis
item.description: Trying to jump ahead of the National League, the American League announces it will add two clubs in 1961 and become a ten-team circuit. The AL admits Los Angeles as an expansion team and permits Calvin Griffith to move his existing Washington Senators franchise, and all its major- and minor-league players, to Minneapolis–Saint Paul.

item.title: 1956: Giants Sign Veteran Slugger Hank Sauer, 40, From Cardinals
item.description: The New York Giants sign veteran slugger Hank Sauer, released by the St. Louis Cardinals. Sauer, at age 40, will make a comeback with the Giants in 1957, hitting 26 homers, tenth in the National League. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1949: Chandler Restores Full World Series Share to Southworth
item.description: After his disgruntled players had voted skipper Billy Southworth, a future Hall-of-Fame manager, only a half-share of the Boston Braves' fourth-place World Series money, Commissioner Happy Chandler steps in to restore Southworth's full amount due. Suffering from stress and rumored to be battling a drinking problem, Southworth took a leave of absence for the last 45 games of the 1949 season. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1946: Pegler Attacks Leo Durocher Over Gambler Ties
item.description: In his nationally syndicated newspaper column, influential journalist and commentator Westbrook Pegler alleges that Leo Durocher is associating with known gamblers and racketeers through his close friendship with actor George Raft. In a series of columns in the coming weeks, Pegler will continue to attack the Brooklyn Dodgers' manager (and Raft) as "threats to society." Photo: Conrad Poirier (Public domain).

item.title: 1931: Charles Comiskey, 72, Hall of Fame First Baseman, Owner
item.description: Charles Comiskey, 72, Hall of Fame first baseman/manager and owner of the Chicago White Sox since the team's formation in 1901, during which time they won four American League pennants and two World Series (1906, 1917), who previously became the first manager to win four consecutive pennants, with the St. Louis Browns (1885–1888), including the 1886 World Series title. and posted the highest winning percentage… Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1911: Athletics Beat Giants 13-2, Win Second Straight Title
item.description: The Philadelphia Athletics defeat the New York Giants, 13–2, in Game 6 of the World Series to win their second consecutive World Championship title. Philadelphia wins the series, four games to two. The six consecutive days of rain between Games 3 and 4 caused the longest delay between World Series games until the Loma Prieta earthquake interrupted the 1989 Series, which incidentally featured the same two franchises… Photo: Bain News Service (Public domain).

item.title: 1909: Frank Siffell, German Catcher for Philadelphia Athletics
item.description: Frank Siffell, German catcher for the Philadelphia Athletics of the American Association (1884–1885).

item.title: 1889: New York Beats Bridegrooms 11-7 in Latest Game
item.description: New York wins again, taking an 11–7 triumph over the Bridegrooms. Photo: J Wood, 208 Bowery, N.Y. (Public domain).

item.title: 1887: Detroit Wins Series 10 Games to 5 Over Browns
item.description: The Browns win the final game of the series, but Detroit wins the series 10 games to 5. Photo: Hastings, George H., fl. 1885-1896, photographer. (Public domain).

item.title: 1877: Devlin and Hall Admit Throwing Games, Implicate Teammates
item.description: Jim Devlin and George Hall are confronted by Louisville vice-president Charles Chase with charges of throwing games. Both players admit to the charges, and also implicate teammates Al Nichols and Bill Craver in the scandal. Photo: Gross & Co (Public domain).

item.title: 1877: Louisville Confronts Hall, Devlin With Game-Throwing Charges
item.description: On October 26, 1877, Louisville club vice president Charles Chase confronted Hall and fellow Gray Jim Devlin with charges that they threw some road games in August and September.
